title: Seedream 5.5 vs Seedream 5.0 Pro: Tested (2026) | Flick
summary: Seedream 5.5 vs Seedream 5.0 Pro: six same-prompt tests and a six-round edit chain on each model, measured on the files, plus Flick prices. Which to use.
body_markdown:
Seedream 5.5 is ByteDance's newest image model, released on November 9, 2026 and on Flick since November 12. Seedream 5.0 Pro is the flagship it follows, on Flick since October 29. ByteDance says 5.5 beats 5.0 Pro in every use case it measured, but two questions matter most for a film: does the text come back right, and does a picture survive being edited again and again?


So we gave both models six identical prompts on Flick, then edited the same film still six rounds on each. Every result is below, measured on the files.


## Quick answer: which should you use?


For most work, Seedream 5.5. In our tests it kept an accent 5.0 Pro dropped, framed a close-up better, held a picture far steadier across six edits, and costs less than half as much. Pick Seedream 5.0 Pro when a poster or page must carry only the words you wrote. To compare them yourself:


1. **Put two image nodes on one canvas,** one per model, at the default 1.5K.
2. **Give both the same prompt,** with every word you want shown in quotes.
3. **Edit each result a few rounds** with "Keep everything else exactly the same", and keep the one that holds.

## How we tested


- Each pair used a byte-identical prompt at each model's default 1.5K, with no reference image and no[Flickpedia style](https://flick.art/docs/visual-styles) .
- One run per model per prompt, so these are single takes, not averages.
- The Seedream 5.0 Pro images are the ones from our[Seedream 5.0 Pro vs GPT Image 2.5](https://flick.art/blog/seedream-5-pro-vs-gpt-image-2-5) test, made on October 30, 2026. The Seedream 5.5 images were made on November 21, 2026.
- For the edit test, both models started from the same Seedream 5.5 image, and each edited its own previous result. We traced every input on the canvas to make sure.
- We read every image at full size and checked each quoted word letter by letter.


## Test 1: a film still lit by one lamp


Prompt:` Cinematic film still, close-up of an old lighthouse keeper with a weathered face and grey stubble, lit by a single oil lamp at night, rain on the window behind him, shallow depth of field, 35mm film grain`


Left, Seedream 5.5: a head and shoulders close-up of an old keeper with a grey beard, an oil lamp at the edge. Right, Seedream 5.0 Pro: the keeper seen from the waist up by a rainy window, an oil lamp, a whisky glass and charts on the table


- **Seedream 5.5** came closer to the close-up asked for, filling the frame with his face, but grew the stubble into a full grey beard.
- **Seedream 5.0 Pro** kept the stubble and added a compass, charts, a whisky glass and a lighthouse beam through the window, none of which the prompt named.
- **Neither added text.**


## Test 2: a poster with a title and tagline


Prompt:` A vintage sci-fi movie poster. Title at the top in bold condensed letters: "THE LAST LIGHTHOUSE". Tagline at the bottom: "Every light goes out eventually." A lone lighthouse on a cliff under a green aurora, a small credits block under the tagline.`


Two vintage posters of a lighthouse under a green aurora. Left, Seedream 5.5: a pale title, extra taglines, studio logos and a long credits block. Right, Seedream 5.0 Pro: a cream title, the tagline and a three-line credits block


- **Both spelled** the title and tagline exactly.
- **Seedream 5.5** added "A SCI-FI MOVIE", two side taglines, two studio logos and an eight-line credits block; the bottom three lines are unreadable.
- **Seedream 5.0 Pro** wrote three clean credit lines, "DIRECTED BY J. HALE" among them, and nothing else.
- **Both invented names,** so check every credit before you print.


## Test 3: Japanese and English on one sign


Prompt:` A narrow Tokyo side street at night, rain on the asphalt. A small café's lit sign reads "夜明けの喫茶店" in large letters with "Dawn Café" underneath, and a chalkboard by the door reads "Coffee 500円". Cinematic, 35mm.`


Two rainy Tokyo lanes at night with a lit café sign in Japanese and English. Left, Seedream 5.5: an empty shopfront and a chalkboard. Right, Seedream 5.0 Pro: an old man behind the window and a chalkboard


- **Both wrote** "夜明けの喫茶店" correctly.
- **Seedream 5.5 kept the accent** in "Dawn Café"; Seedream 5.0 Pro wrote "Dawn Cafe".
- **Seedream 5.5** split the chalkboard into "Coffee" and "500円" with some scribbled small print between; 5.0 Pro wrote it cleanly and added an old man at work behind the window.


## Test 4: a six-panel comic page


Prompt:` A full comic book page with six panels in a 2 by 3 grid, clean black gutters. A girl and her robot dog search a flooded city for a lost kite. Speech balloons: panel 1 "It flew this way!", panel 3 "Woof?", panel 6 "Found it!". Inked lines, flat colors.`


Two six-panel comic pages of a girl in pink and a robot dog in a flooded city. Left, Seedream 5.5: two rows of three panels with extra balloons and signs. Right, Seedream 5.0 Pro: two columns of three numbered panels


- **Both put the three lines** in panels 1, 3 and 6, spelled correctly, and neither drew the black gutters asked for.
- **Seedream 5.5** repeated "It flew this way!" in panels 2, 4 and 5 and painted three signs, one reading "SIGN STRONGER OVER HERE...".
- **Seedream 5.0 Pro** numbered the panels 1 to 6 and added one "RAMEN" billboard with unreadable small print.


## Test 5: a watercolour picture book page


Prompt:` A children's picture book illustration in soft watercolor and pencil: a fox reading a map by lantern light in a snowy forest, warm and cold colors, lots of white paper showing.`


Two watercolour foxes in snow. Left, Seedream 5.5: a fox in glasses and a scarf by a lantern and campfire, lots of white paper and a caption above. Right, Seedream 5.0 Pro: a fluffy fox over a map beside a lantern under a blue grey sky


- **Measured on the files:** near-white pixels, paper or snow, cover 43% of Seedream 5.5's picture against 22% of Seedream 5.0 Pro's, and 65% against 2% in the top half, where the sky is.
- **Seedream 5.5** followed "lots of white paper" but wrote a four-line story caption and labelled a crate, a tin and two trail signs.
- **Seedream 5.0 Pro** painted a fuller scene with a blue grey wash and no text.


## Test 6: a storyboard sheet with labels


Prompt:` A film storyboard sheet with four panels in a row, each with a hand-drawn sketch and a typed label underneath: "1. WIDE - harbor at dawn", "2. MEDIUM - fisherman pulls the net", "3. CLOSE - a glowing fish", "4. OVER THE SHOULDER - the town watches". Pencil on white paper.`


Two pencil storyboards of four panels: a harbor, a fisherman with a net, a fish, a man facing a town. Left, Seedream 5.5: taller detailed panels with serif labels. Right, Seedream 5.0 Pro: square panels, typewriter labels and a glowing fish


- **Both typed** every word of the four labels.
- **Seedream 5.0 Pro** kept the hyphens and made the fish glow as a bright white burst.
- **Seedream 5.5** drew each hyphen as a longer spaced dash and gave the fish a sparkle rather than a glow.


## Test 7: six edits in a row


This is the claim ByteDance leads with. We gave both editors the same six requests in the same order, each fed the previous result: a wool cap, the lamp swapped for a candle, a cream sweater, wire glasses, a turn to camera, a red scarf. Every prompt ended with "Keep everything else exactly the same."


Seedream 5.5, six rounds of edits on the lighthouse keeper: a cap, a candle, a cream sweater, glasses, a turn to camera, a red scarf, the window and light unchanged Seedream 5.0 Pro, the same six rounds: a cap, a taller candle with its reflection now in the window, a cream sweater, glasses, a turn to camera, a red scarf


Both made every change in the round it was asked for. The difference is in what they were told to leave alone. We measured two patches of the window that no prompt touched, in levels out of 255:


Seedream 5.5 Seedream 5.0 Pro


Per round, left window 0.7 to 0.8 2.0 to 7.0


Per round, right window 0.6 to 0.7 1.0 to 2.5


After six rounds, left window 3.0 14.9


After six rounds, right window 3.1 6.1


- **Seedream 5.5 drifted two to five times less,** close to the noise of saving a JPEG again.
- **Seedream 5.0 Pro changed the window** in round 2, adding the candle's reflected flame to the glass: the biggest single jump in our measure.
- **By the end,** the face on Seedream 5.0 Pro is lit in a cooler tone with a whiter beard, while Seedream 5.5 kept the warm candlelight.


The six edits cost 54 credits on Seedream 5.5 (9 each) and 84 on Seedream 5.0 Pro (14 each).


## Which should you use?


- **Seedream 5.5 for repeated edits.** Its untouched areas moved about 3 levels in total over six rounds, against up to 14.9 for 5.0 Pro.
- **Seedream 5.5 for a lower price.** 6 credits a new image against 14, and 9 an edit against 14, at the same size.
- **Seedream 5.5 for cut-outs.** Only it has a Transparent Background setting. See our[Seedream 5.5 guide](https://flick.art/blog/seedream-5-5-guide) for how it handles glass and glows.
- **Seedream 5.0 Pro for clean text.** It added one billboard and a short credits block across six tests, where 5.5 added taglines, logos, signs and a caption.


These are single takes, so run your own pair before you commit a whole film to one model.[Choosing a model](https://flick.art/docs/choosing-a-model) has more on comparing fairly.

## Frequently Asked Questions


Is Seedream 5.5 better than Seedream 5.0 Pro?


For most work in our tests, yes: it kept an accent 5.0 Pro dropped, framed a close-up better, edited more steadily and costs less. Seedream 5.0 Pro added much less unrequested text.


Which is cheaper, Seedream 5.5 or Seedream 5.0 Pro?


Seedream 5.5: 6 credits a new image on Flick against 14 for Seedream 5.0 Pro, and 9 an edit against 14. See Model credit costs.


Does Seedream 5.0 Pro support transparent backgrounds?


Not on Flick. The Transparent Background setting is on Seedream 5.5, which introduced native transparent output.


Is there a Seedream 5.5 Pro?


ByteDance says a Pro version of Seedream 5.5 will follow, with no date as of November 21, 2026. Today's Pro model on Flick is Seedream 5.0 Pro.


Do both models take reference images?


Yes, up to 10 each on Flick. In Edit Image, both read several references when the prompt calls them Figure 1, Figure 2 and so on.


Can I use both for free?


Both are on Flick's Free plan, and each image uses credits. A new account gets 100 credits, and free accounts get 100 more each day.
